# Operating a run

**GENERATED by `.github/scripts/operator.mjs` from the workflow contracts, the gate model, the
scripts register and the run tree. Never edit it — `C144` fails when it drifts.** Regenerate with
`node .github/scripts/operator.mjs --write`.

This page is for whoever operates a run by hand, which is not the person the workflow talks to.
The workflow makes these moves itself: agents write the documents and trigger the tasks, and the
tasks run the scripts. This page gives, as commands, the moves that take a run from one stage to
the next and the moves inside a stage that those depend on. The other tasks a person runs, such as
adding a problem in their own words, recording an edit or keeping a stale stage, are described in
`specifications/onboarding/TASKS.md`.

**Substitute `{runs_root}` yourself.** Its one line is in `.github/runs-root`. Every command below
carries the placeholder for the same reason every skill contract does: the value differs per
recipient and a page generated against one of them would be wrong everywhere else.

**`<run_id>` is the run identifier**, in the `{year}-{month}-{slug}` shape stage 1 assigns. The
run-state commands take the identifier; the check commands take the directory.

---

## Starting a run

One command. It creates the whole tree — the 7 stage folders, their
`records/`, `read/`, the run record and a generated front page. **Nobody is ever asked to create a
folder**, and if one you were told to write into is missing, the run was not initialised.

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs init <run_id>
```

---

## The seven stages

**Every stage is the same five moves**: mark it running, let the agent produce, record what it
wrote, run the gate, record the gate. Stages with a decision gate add a person between the two.

**Five stages also have a move inside the stage.**

At stage 2, before the agent writes, the problem-material record is written from the files a person
put in `2-problems/supplied/`, without reading them; the agent is instructed to run this as a task.
Once the stage is produced, the driver writes each supplied file's measurement onto the items that
cite it, after the scripts listed under stage 2 below and before Q2. That list leaves the second out:

```bash
node .github/scripts/problem-material.mjs <run_id> --write
node .github/scripts/problem-material.mjs <run_id> --measure
```

At stage 3, where a person put a market list in `3-competitive-analysis/supplied/`, the agent is
instructed to record it on the run before it works from that list:

```bash
node .github/scripts/market-material.mjs <run_id> --write
```

Where the folder is empty there is nothing to record, and that command refuses. The agent searches if
VS Code's web search extension and a search key are installed, and otherwise works from web addresses
a person supplies.

**Stage 4 takes its own route after the agent has written A8, and the `produced`, `G4` and `accepted`
lines under stage 4 below do not work for it.** Followed as written they accept the stage while A9,
the selected-solution document, is never written, and `C112` fails. A9 carries the reason for the
person's choice, and only the approval writes it. After marking stage 4 running and once A8 is written,
run these instead. The first records the stage as produced, runs the stage's scripts and Q4, and puts
the stage in review; the second records the person's choice; the third records G4 in their name,
writes A9 from the choice and accepts the stage:

```bash
node .github/scripts/advance.mjs <run_id>
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs decide <run_id> 4 --kind choice --selection <solution id> --what "<why, in their words>" --by "<name>" --role <role>
node .github/scripts/advance.mjs <run_id> --approve --by "<name>" --role <role>
```

At stage 5 a person chooses one MVP option while the stage is being written, before it is recorded as
produced, because the expansion is written for the option they chose. At stage 6 a person marks the
draft PRD agreed, and the agreed PRD is written from the draft word for word. Record each in the
person's name:

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs decide <run_id> 5 --kind choice --selection <option id> --what "<why, in their words>" --by "<name>" --role <role>
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs agree <run_id> 6 --by "<name>"
```

### Stage 1 — Brief

**Who:** .github/agents/product-manager.agent.md · **Writes into:** `{runs_root}/<run_id>/1-brief/` · **Produces:** A1

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs stage <run_id> 1 running
```

Invoke the agent. When it says what it wrote, record it — one `--artifact` per artifact, and
one `--know-how` per body it read, at the version it read:

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs stage <run_id> 1 produced --artifact A1 --know-how <body>@<version>
```

Run the gate. **No agent runs its own gate** — the checker has to be independent of the producer:

```bash
node .github/scripts/check.mjs {runs_root}/<run_id> --gate Q1
```

It returns `pass`, `fail` or `incomplete`, and `incomplete` is not a pass. **Add `--record` and
the verdict it computed is written for you**, through the same writer every other move goes
through — so what lands on the record is what the gate found rather than what you typed:

```bash
node .github/scripts/check.mjs {runs_root}/<run_id> --gate Q1 --record --by "check.mjs, run independently of the producer"
```

An `incomplete` gate refuses to record: there is no verdict, and writing it as a fail would say
a check found something wrong. Recording by hand is still there when you need it:

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs gate <run_id> 1 Q1 pass --by "check.mjs, run independently of the producer"
```

Now a person decides. Put the stage in front of them, and record the decision in their name:

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs stage <run_id> 1 in_review
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs gate <run_id> 1 G1 pass --by "<the person's name>"
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs stage <run_id> 1 accepted
```

Then regenerate the front door, so the run says where it is:

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-readme.mjs {runs_root}/<run_id> --write
```

## When a gate fails

**A stage that fails its quality gate does not reach a person.** It returns to the skill. The
writer moves the stage to `q_failed` on its own when you record a failing gate, and refuses
`accepted` from there. **The exception is a failure about a stage already accepted**, which the
skill cannot change from here: when every check that failed is about one, the person is asked to
sign it off, as below, unless one of those checks is one nobody can sign, or an earlier accepted stage's
sign-off over the same finding already carries to it, which the gate's closing names.

**Unless a person signs what the run cannot satisfy.** `SPOCK: sign off a check this run cannot
meet` records the check or checks one gate run failed, on one stage, with one reason in the
signer's own words — `C11` alone, or `C11,C12,C171` where one cause failed several. **It may name
only what that gate recorded as failing**, and the writer refuses the rest. Where every check the gate
recorded as failing is signed, the stage stays `produced` and advances from there, and **the gate
result stays `fail` on the record, on the front page and in every report that reads them**, with the
signed exception recorded beside it. The checks that keep the record honest cannot be signed at all.

**The signature works just as well after the stage has parked.** A stage sitting at `q_failed`
moves to `in_review` once every check its gate recorded as failing is signed, and it is the same
signature and the same task — nothing has to be undone first. **Do not send it back to `running`
to try again**: that edge is for work being rewritten, and it withdraws the signatures the stage
was carrying, which is how a run can park, be signed, and park again.

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs gate <run_id> <stage> <Qn> fail --by "check.mjs, run independently of the producer"
```

When a person sends a stage back rather than a check, record it in their name and role, with their reason.
It ends the stage's acceptance and its gate result, withdraws its decisions and the answers to its gate's questions
and keeps them on the record, and marks the later stages built
on it stale:

```bash
node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs retract <run_id> <stage> --by "<name>" --role "<role>" --reason "<why>"
```

---

## The whole run, and what it produced

```bash
node .github/scripts/check.mjs {runs_root}/<run_id>
```

Every check the build implements, over the whole run. A run holding no artifact returns
`incomplete` and says so, because a gate cannot pass on a run that has produced nothing.
On a run started on build 1.12 or later, a document of an accepted stage edited with no edit recorded is
listed after the tally under *Reported, not a failure*, with the send-back and the edit task; it changes
neither the tally nor the exit code.

```bash
node .github/scripts/check.mjs {runs_root}/<run_id> --gates
```

Which of the seven gates this build can run in full, and which half of each one ran.

```bash
node .github/scripts/check.mjs {runs_root}/<run_id> --document A8
```

**Everything the checks say about one document, and nothing about the rest of the run.** It is
the shortest loop this build has.

---

## Every command, and what it is for

Generated from `.github/registry/scripts.yaml`. **What is not here is not yours to run**: the
rest of `.github/scripts/` is either a library nothing invokes directly or the harness this
repository proves itself with.

| Command | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `node .github/scripts/advance.mjs` | Makes every mechanical move between one human decision and the next on the open run (moves the stage, runs the stage's scripts, runs and records the quality gate, accepts or stops) and names whose decision is owed; with `--approve` it records the person's approval in their name, and `--waits` only prints what the stage waits on from a person. |
| `node .github/scripts/run-state.mjs` | The single writer of a run's record: it starts a run and records each stage move, gate result, decision, sign-off, agreement, correction and stop. |
| `node .github/scripts/check.mjs` | Runs the quality checks over one run's documents and record and reports, gate by gate, which pass, which fail and what passing looks like. |
| `node .github/scripts/explain.mjs` | Prints, for each check the open stage's gate fails now, what failed, what the check is for and why from its card in COVERAGE-CHECKS.md, what passes and what to do, and its section in the stage's shapes body where it has one, grouped by the document each failure is about. |
| `node .github/scripts/card-join.mjs` | Assembles stage 3's competitor cards document from the card parts word for word, so the join cannot mistranscribe; without `--write` it reports how the document differs from its parts. |
| `node .github/scripts/derive.mjs` | Turns each stage 4 solution's answers to the compliance area cards' questions into the compliance section a person reads, printing every fired touchpoint as its card wrote it; without `--write` it reports what it would write. |
| `node .github/scripts/solution-join.mjs` | Assembles stage 4's solution set from its parts word for word behind one index table, and writes the selected solution from the person's recorded choice; without `--write` it reports the difference. |
| `node .github/scripts/fanout.mjs` | Writes the briefs for stage 4's fan-out, read from the contract's `invocations:`: the slate brief that names the set, one author brief per slate entry, and the join brief. It writes briefs, never documents. |
| `node .github/scripts/task.mjs` | Runs a task's scripts in order: it applies each box's refusal before any script runs, hands the box values to the scripts through the environment, stops the chain at the first failure, prints the output and keeps all of it in `.github/last-task.md`. |
| `node .github/scripts/update.mjs` | Moves a tester's copy of the workflow to the lab's latest release without a merge, keeping the runs, the two local settings and the competitors kept on that copy. |
| `node .github/scripts/setup-check.mjs` | Says line by line whether this computer has what SPOCK needs (VS Code, the chat tool, the agents, the build, git and the update source) and ends on a numbered list of what to do when something is missing. |
| `node .github/scripts/facts.mjs` | Prints what this build can state about itself (counts of skills, agents, checks, know-how bodies and more), each computed from the build with where it comes from. |
| `node .github/scripts/material.mjs` | Lists what a run's problem material folder holds and which of it the agent can open directly. |
| `node .github/scripts/promote-competitors.mjs` | Keeps a finished run's competitor cards, so the committed competitor store learns from the run. |
| `node .github/scripts/written.mjs` | Lists what the stage in progress has written so far and what the checks say about each document, before the stage's gate can decide the whole stage; on a run started on 1.16.1 or later it reads the stage's envelope as `envelope.mjs` computes it and names what that refuses. |
| `node .github/scripts/convert.mjs` | Turns every Word, PowerPoint, Excel and PDF file a run was given into text beside the original, with nothing installed and nothing replaced; a PDF is read whole or refused with its reason and the route through Word. |
| `node .github/scripts/metrics.mjs` | Reports how the workflow performed, read from what the run records already say: gate dates, refinement rounds, superseded documents, declared gaps and answered questions, against the baseline record. |
| `node .github/scripts/trace.mjs` | Reduces a raw OpenTelemetry trace file that VS Code Copilot Chat wrote to the spans `.github/registry/tracing.yaml` declares, grouped by run, and shows what a run already carries. |
| `node .github/scripts/template-diff.mjs` | Shows a document against the template it was written to, as a diff, for the person at the decision gate: the PRD against the PRD template and the initiative against the initiative template. |
| `node .github/scripts/pasted.mjs` | Takes what a person pasted in the chat into the run as theirs: problem material at stage 2, a market list at stage 3, recorded as the person's supply. |
| `node .github/scripts/withdraw.mjs` | Takes back a file or a stage's files from a run as a workflow act with a trail: nothing is deleted, and a folder named is listed before anything moves. |
| `node .github/scripts/hand-edit.mjs` | Records a person's own change to a document as theirs: it marks the document `modified_by: human` and adds an account of what they changed, why and who they are. |
| `node .github/scripts/keep.mjs` | Keeps a later stage as it is after a stage it is built on was sent back and accepted again, once every stage it is built on is accepted, as the person's recorded decision. |

**Generated surfaces.** Each writes a file something else reads, and each has a check that fails
when the file and the generator disagree. Never edit what they produce.

| Command | What it writes |
|---|---|
| `node .github/scripts/assemble.mjs` | Fills the envelope of the documents and records a stage has written, as `envelope.mjs` computes it from the contract, the registry and the field spec. On a run started on 1.16.1 or later `--write` writes nothing while the stage is being written and says what is written at approval, and `--finalise` writes a stage once it is accepted; on an earlier run `--write` fills it as before. Never the body, except the section headings of the initiative and the PRD in the run's language, never the content fields a gate decides, and the decision block only from the decision the run records. |
| `node .github/scripts/problem-material.mjs` | Writes stage 2's problem-material record from what the person actually supplied (files, pasted text, a problem in their own words), with each item's source, size and period, and measures items not yet measured. |
| `node .github/scripts/market-material.mjs` | Records on the run record the market list a person supplied in place of a stage 3 web search: its file name, size, hash and how many competitors and trends it holds, counted from its headings without reading what the entries say. |
| `node .github/scripts/task-page.mjs` | Writes `specifications/onboarding/TASKS.md`, the page saying what every task a person can run does, from `.vscode/tasks.json`. |
| `node .github/scripts/run-readme.mjs` | Writes a run's front page (README.md) from the run it describes: what it produced, where each stage stands, what it waits on and what to read first. |
| `node .github/scripts/reading-copy.mjs` | Writes the reading copy of the initiative, the one document Česká spořitelna is handed, from the initiative with its machine record stripped. |
| `node .github/scripts/agent-descriptions.mjs` | Writes each agent's description, the line the agent picker shows: its purpose and trigger phrases from `agents.yaml`, and between them, from the registry, the documents it works from and writes, by their names, whether it reaches outside the repository and its tools. |
| `node .github/scripts/store.mjs` | Rebuilds the competitor store from the committed example runs and the runs a person kept with `SPOCK: keep this run's competitors`; a stage writes what it finds into its own run, never into the store. |
| `node .github/scripts/know-how.mjs` | Writes the build's know-how tree `.github/know-how/` from its source of record, `specifications/definitions/know-how/`. |
| `node .github/scripts/fixed-messages.mjs` | Holds the workflow's fixed messages, gate questions and the words a check reads, in English and in Czech, in one table, and writes the Czech block under each English message in the files that show one. |
| `node .github/scripts/regmap.mjs` | Writes `specifications/REGMAP.md`, the regulatory map, from `.github/registry/regmap.yaml` and the skills' bindings. |
| `node .github/scripts/signpost.mjs` | Writes `specifications/DOCUMENTATION.md`, every document a person can read and which of them a person may edit. |
| `node .github/scripts/content-register.mjs` | Writes `specifications/CONTENT-REGISTER.md`, what this build is made of, joined from the registries that already hold it. |
| `node .github/scripts/register.mjs` | Writes `.github/COVERAGE-CHECKS.md`, one card per registered check, joining the hand-written cards with where the gates run each check and what passes; `--verify` reconciles §7.4, the gate model, the checker, the shapes and the cards and refuses any disagreement. |
| `node .github/scripts/floor.mjs` | Writes `.github/composed-behaviours.yaml`, the composed-behaviour carrier, from `COMPOSED_FLOOR` in the gate model. |
| `node .github/scripts/artifact-fields.mjs` | Writes `.github/artifact-fields.yaml`, the field set of every artifact, read from §6 of the business logic, and prints one artifact's set on request. |
| `node .github/scripts/unverified.mjs` | Writes `.github/could-not-verify.yaml`, the rules each skill's gate cannot verify mechanically, which every artifact carries, from the gate model. |
| `node .github/scripts/operator.mjs` | Writes `.github/OPERATING-A-RUN.md`, the page for whoever operates a run by hand, from the workflow contracts, the gate model, this register and the run tree. |
| `node .github/scripts/release-files.mjs` | Writes the release's list of its own files with their hashes, and holds the comparison C189 and the update make against it. |
